mainTopic: Yoma 14b: אביי on רבי עקיבא and the הזאה, and the dispute over whether the קטורת or the נרות comes first
overview: This amud opens by finishing a source about the water used for הזאה. אביי then shows that our משנה can fit even רבי עקיבא's view: they sprinkle on the כהן גדול toward evening, so he is pure again by the next day. The גמרא next asks why our משנה puts the קטורת before cleaning the נרות, while מסכת תמיד puts the מנורה first. רב הונא's answer that תמיד follows רבי שמעון איש המצפה is rejected, and רבי יוחנן says instead that סדר יומא follows him. The same contradiction then appears between two משניות inside יומא itself. אביי answers that the lamps were cleaned in two stages: five lamps before the קטורת and two lamps after it. When this is challenged from אביי's own list of the daily service, the גמרא answers that the list follows אבא שאול and our משנה follows the רבנן, as a ברייתא records. The amud ends with אבא שאול's source in the פסוק and the start of the רבנן's reading of that פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words of the source about the minimum water needed
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the quoted source: there must be enough water to dip the tops of the stems and sprinkle.
steps.simpleTranslation: …the tops of the stems and sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: These words finish a source quoted at the end of the previous section. That source requires enough water in the vessel to dip the tips of the אזוב and sprinkle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source comes from מסכת פרה. It shows that even the view that the sprinkling itself has no minimum amount agrees that the vessel must hold a minimum amount of water. Here the גמרא is only finishing that quote before moving on.

keyTerms.meaning: The tops of the stems (of the אזוב / hyssop)
And he sprinkles (from הַזָּאָה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the end of a quote that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: the tops of the stems, and sprinkle.
phrases.notes: End of the quote from משנה פרה: the vessel needs enough water to dip the stem tips.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source citation begun earlier.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a minimum amount of water required in the vessel
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת פרה about dipping the tops of the stems

steps.title: אביי: sprinkle on the High Priest toward evening
steps.stepSummary: אביי says our משנה can follow even רבי עקיבא. They sprinkle on the כהן גדול toward evening, after his day of service, so he can immerse and become pure by sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say this follows רבי עקיבא. The כהן גדול does the service all day, toward evening they sprinkle on him, and he immerses and waits for sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the earlier problem that our משנה seemed not to fit רבי עקיבא. He explains that the timing of the sprinkling solves the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that הזאה water makes a pure person impure. If they sprinkled in the morning, a pure כהן גדול would become impure and could not serve that day. Sprinkling in the evening avoids this: he finishes the day's עבודה, immerses, and is pure again after sunset, ready for the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say
Toward evening
They sprinkle on him
He immerses (טְבִילָה)
Sunset, which completes the purification after טבילה

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the כהן גדול's sprinkling happens in the evening. That way, even under רבי עקיבא's view, any impurity it causes is gone by the next day's service.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the order and timing of a procedure can reconcile a משנה with a תנא who seemed to disagree with it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if you say it is Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא holds that the sprinkling water makes the pure impure.

phrases.english: for he performs the service the whole day,
and toward evening they sprinkle on him,
and he immerses and waits for sunset.
phrases.notes: So he is pure for the next morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier difficulty about רבי עקיבא and resolves it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the timing of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, because sprinkling would make the pure כהן גדול impure and unable to serve.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the sprinkling is done in the evening, the כהן גדול immerses and is pure by the next day, so even רבי עקיבא can agree.

steps.title: Our משנה implies incense comes before the lamps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which lists burning the קטורת before cleaning the נרות, and infers that the קטורת comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he burns the incense and cleans the lamps.' So the incense comes first and then the lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting our משנה and drawing an inference about the order. This step sets up a contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two daily tasks the כהן גדול practices during his seven days of preparation. From the order of the words, the גמרא infers that the קטורת is done before the הטבת הנרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Burns the incense
Cleans and prepares the lamps of the מנורה (הֲטָבַת הַנֵּרוֹת)
Apparently / this shows that
First

phrases.english: And he burns the incense
phrases.notes: Quote from our משנה.

phrases.english: and cleans the lamps.
Apparently the incense comes first
and then the lamps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the order of the daily Temple tasks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to our משנה, the קטורת comes before the הטבת הנרות.

steps.title: Contradiction from מסכת תמיד: the מנורה comes before the incense
steps.stepSummary: The order of the lottery in מסכת תמיד is: ashes of the inner altar, then the מנורה, then the קטורת. That puts the lamps before the incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradict it: 'The one who won the clearing of the inner altar, the one who won the מנורה, and the one who won the incense.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction from a משנה in מסכת תמיד, which lists the מנורה before the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lottery in מסכת תמיד follows the order in which the tasks are actually done. There the lamps come before the incense, which is the opposite of the order inferred from our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it: introduces a contradiction between two sources
Won the lottery for a task
Removing the ashes from the inner (golden) altar
The candelabrum

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
The one who won the clearing of ashes from the inner altar,
phrases.notes: From מסכת תמיד.

phrases.english: and the one who won the menorah,
and the one who won the incense!
phrases.notes: Here the lamps come before the incense.

steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the קטורת comes before the נרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two משניות: מסכת תמיד lists the מנורה before the קטורת.

steps.title: רב הונא: תמיד follows רבי שמעון איש המצפה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that מסכת תמיד was taught by רבי שמעון איש המצפה, a different תנא from the author of our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Who taught מסכת תמיד? It is רבי שמעון איש המצפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא settles the contradiction by saying the two משניות come from different תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing the two sources to agree, רב הונא assigns them to different authors. מסכת תמיד, which puts the lamps first, follows רבי שמעון איש המצפה, while our משנה follows another view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this? (identifying the author)
מסכת תמיד, the tractate about the daily offering service
The תנא whom רב הונא names as the author of תמיד

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Who taught Tamid?
It is Rabbi Shimon Ish HaMitzpa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאן תָּנָא תָּמִיד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the sources to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות should follow one view, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: מסכת תמיד follows רבי שמעון איש המצפה, so it may disagree with our משנה.

steps.title: Challenge: we know רבי שמעון איש המצפה holds the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we know רבי שמעון איש המצפה disagrees with the anonymous משנה in תמיד. It first quotes that משנה about where the blood is placed on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard the opposite from him! As we learned: He comes to the northeast corner and places blood on the northeast; then at the southwest corner he places blood on the southwest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. It first quotes the anonymous משנה in תמיד about placing the blood of the תמיד. The next step will show that רבי שמעון איש המצפה argues with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous משנה says one placement of blood on each of the two diagonal corners, like any עולה. This sets up the proof that רבי שמעון איש המצפה holds differently, which would mean he is not the author of the anonymous משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard the opposite from him
As we learned in a משנה
The northeast corner of the altar
Places (the blood)

phrases.english: But we have heard the opposite from him,
as we learned:
He comes to the northeast corner,
he places blood on the northeast;
at the southwest corner,
he places blood on the southwest.
phrases.notes: A single placement at the corner, like a regular עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's attribution in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the anonymous משניות in תמיד follow רבי שמעון איש המצפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי שמעון איש המצפה disagrees with an anonymous משנה in תמיד, he cannot be its author.

steps.title: The ברייתא shows רבי שמעון איש המצפה disagrees with תמיד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on that משנה says רבי שמעון איש המצפה changes the procedure for the תמיד: at the southwest corner he places blood on the west and then on the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught about it: רבי שמעון איש המצפה changes the procedure for the תמיד. At the northeast corner he places blood on the northeast. At the southwest corner he places blood on the west, and afterward on the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof for its challenge. This ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון איש המצפה disagrees with the anonymous משנה in תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous משנה says one placement at the southwest corner. רבי שמעון איש המצפה requires two separate placements there, west and then south. Since he argues with the anonymous משנה, he cannot be the anonymous author of תמיד, and this undercuts רב הונא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught about it (a ברייתא on the משנה)
Changes the procedure for the daily offering
And afterward

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree about the northeast corner. The disagreement is only at the southwest corner: one placement according to the anonymous משנה, two separate ones according to רבי שמעון איש המצפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא tests a claim about who authored a משנה: if the proposed author disagrees with that משנה elsewhere, the claim is in trouble.

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ הַמִּצְפָּה מְשַׁנֶּה בַּתָּמִיד:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Ish HaMitzpa changes the procedure for the daily offering:
at the northeast corner,
he places blood on the northeast.
phrases.notes: This is the same as the משנה that doesn't name who said it.

phrases.english: At the southwest corner,
he places blood on the west,
and afterward places blood on the south.
phrases.notes: Two separate placements, unlike the משנה that doesn't name who said it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנֵי עֲלַהּ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ הַמִּצְפָּה מְשַׁנֶּה בַּתָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof that completes the challenge in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון איש המצפה is not the author of the anonymous משניות in תמיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the משנה in תמיד about the placement of the blood

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: סדר יומא Follows רבי שמעון איש המצפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reverses רב הונא's answer. The author of סדר יומא is רבי שמעון איש המצפה, and the anonymous מסכת תמיד follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: Who taught the Order of the Day (סדר יומא)? It is רבי שמעון איש המצפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא's answer failed, so the גמרא brings a new answer. רבי יוחנן says it is our משנה in יומא, not תמיד, that follows רבי שמעון איש המצפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps showed that רבי שמעון איש המצפה argues with the anonymous משנה in תמיד, so תמיד cannot be his. רבי יוחנן keeps the idea of two different תנאים but switches them around. סדר יומא is רבי שמעון איש המצפה, and תמיד is the רבנן. That explains why the two give a different order for the קטורת and the נרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is rejected and a new one is coming.
The Order of the Day, meaning the משניות describing the יום כיפור service in מסכת יומא
Who taught? A question about which תנא authored a teaching

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: אלא means the previous answer of רב הונא is dropped.

phrases.english: Who taught the Order of the Day (Yoma)?
It is Rabbi Shimon Ish HaMitzpa.
phrases.notes: So the משנה in תמיד that doesn't name who said it follows the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאן תְּנָא סֵדֶר יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב הונא's answer (Step 5) after Steps 6-7 showed that תמיד cannot be רבי שמעון איש המצפה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא thought מסכת תמיד was authored by רבי שמעון איש המצפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: סדר יומא is by רבי שמעון איש המצפה, and תמיד follows the רבנן. That is why their orders differ.

steps.title: A Contradiction Between Two משניות Within יומא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to a different משנה in יומא itself about the daily lotteries. There the מנורה is cleaned in the second lottery, before the קטורת in the third lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא sets one משנה in יומא against another משנה in יומא. We learned: The second lottery decided who slaughters, who throws the blood, who clears the inner altar, who cleans the מנורה, and who brings the limbs up to the ramp. Then came the third lottery: 'Those new to the קטורת, come and join the lottery!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer by quoting a second משנה from יומא. That משנה puts cleaning the מנורה before the קטורת, which contradicts our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן solved the problem by assigning יומא and תמיד to different תנאים. Now both conflicting sources are in סדר יומא. In the lottery משנה, the מנורה is handled in the second lottery and the קטורת only in the third. That means lamps first and incense second, the opposite of our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he threw. It means the גמרא sets one source against another to show they contradict.
A lottery used to decide which כהן does each job
Clears out the ashes, or the burnt wicks of the מנורה
The ramp leading up to the outer מזבח
Priests who have never offered the קטורת before

steps.confusionAlert: The lottery משנה is also in מסכת יומא, not in תמיד. That is the whole point of the challenge. Both sources are in the same book, so רבי יוחנן's 'different תנאים' answer cannot fix this.

phrases.english: And he contrasted the Order of Yoma against the Order of Yoma,
as we learned: The second lottery:
who slaughters, who throws the blood,
who clears the ashes of the inner altar,
and who cleans out the Menorah,
phrases.notes: The מנורה appears in the second lottery.

phrases.english: and who brings the limbs up to the ramp.
The third lottery:
'Those new to the incense, come and join the lottery!'
phrases.notes: The קטורת comes only in the third lottery, after the מנורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer by producing a contradiction that exists inside סדר יומא itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's resolution (Step 8), and the order in our משנה (Step 3)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources are in סדר יומא, which רבי יוחנן says is by one תנא. One puts the קטורת before the נרות, and the other puts the נרות before the קטורת. The contradiction remains.

steps.title: אביי: Two Lamps Versus Five Lamps
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the lamps were cleaned in two stages. The lottery משנה means the first five lamps, done before the קטורת. Our משנה means the last two lamps, done after the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here, our משנה means cleaning two lamps. There, the lottery משנה means cleaning five lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by saying the two משניות are talking about different stages of cleaning the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה's seven lamps were not cleaned all at once. Five were done first and the last two later. The five lamps come before the קטורת, which is what the lottery משנה describes. The final two come after the קטורת, which is what our משנה describes. So both משניות are true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. It introduces an answer that removes a contradiction.
Preparing the lamps by cleaning out old wicks and ashes
Here... there. It assigns each source to a different case.

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that the נרות were cleaned in two stages (five, then two) is key for the rest of the sugya. It sets up the next question about what came between the two stages.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
here, it refers to preparing two lamps,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה, talking about the last two lamps, which come after the קטורת.

phrases.english: there, it refers to preparing five lamps.
phrases.notes: This is the lottery משנה, talking about the first five lamps, which come before the קטורת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בַּהֲטָבַת שְׁתֵּי נֵרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (two stages of the same service)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to be talking about cleaning the whole מנורה, so their orders clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five lamps come before the קטורת and the two lamps come after it. Each משנה describes a different stage.

steps.title: אביי's Own List Puts the Blood, Not the Incense, Between the Lamps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer from his own list of the daily service order. That list puts the blood of the תמיד, not the קטורת, between the five lamps and the two lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the קטורת separates the two lamp stages? But אביי, when he laid out the order of the daily service based on tradition, said the blood of the תמיד separates them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions אביי's answer by pointing to a different teaching of his. There, something else comes between the two stages of the lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer suggests that the קטורת comes between the five lamps and the two lamps. In his famous list of the daily order, received by tradition, the sprinkling of the blood of the תמיד is what comes between them. In that list the two lamps still come before the קטורת. So אביי seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? It introduces a troubling conclusion that seems to follow
Separates, or comes in between
Laid out the order of the daily service in the מקדש
In the name of tradition, meaning a received teaching
The blood of the daily תמיד offering

phrases.english: Is that to say that the incense separates them?
But Abaye laid out the order of the daily service
in the name of tradition,
and he said the blood of the daily offering separates them!
phrases.notes: In אביי's list, the two lamps still come before the קטורת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer from Step 10 using his own teaching elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer that the קטורת comes between the five lamps and the two lamps
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's traditional list puts the blood of the תמיד between the lamp stages, and in it all the lamps come before the קטורת. That clashes with the answer that the קטורת separates them.

steps.title: אביי's List Follows אבא שאול, Our משנה Follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the two sources follow different opinions. אביי's list follows אבא שאול, and our משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It is not difficult. That list follows אבא שאול, and this משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי's list and our משנה follow two different תנאים who disagree about the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's list, where all the lamps come before the קטורת, follows אבא שאול. Our משנה, where the קטורת comes before the last two lamps, follows the רבנן. אביי's two-stage answer works for the רבנן. His list simply records the opinion of אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: They say. An anonymous answer given by the Sages of the academy
That one... this one. It assigns each source to a different opinion.
A תנא who disagrees with the רבנן here

phrases.english: They say: It is not difficult:
that list follows Abba Shaul,
phrases.notes: אביי's order of the daily service.

phrases.english: this follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is our משנה, where the קטורת comes before the last two lamps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָא קַשְׁיָא הָהִיא לְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל הָא לְרַבָּנַן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's list and our משנה should agree, so the two-stage answer seems to contradict his list.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי's list follows אבא שאול, and our משנה follows the רבנן. They simply hold different views.

steps.title: The ברייתא Where the רבנן and אבא שאול Disagree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves the disagreement. The רבנן say to burn the קטורת first and then clean the lamps, while אבא שאול says to clean the lamps first and then burn the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One should not clean the lamps and then burn the incense. Rather, he should burn the incense and then clean the lamps. אבא שאול says: He cleans the lamps and then burns the incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the רבנן and אבא שאול really do disagree about this order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous first opinion, the רבנן, says the קטורת comes first. That matches our משנה. אבא שאול says the lamps come first. That matches אביי's list. This confirms the answer in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
He should prepare or clean the lamps
He should burn the incense

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the קטורת and the נרות is a dispute among תנאים. The רבנן (our משנה) say the קטורת comes first, then the last two lamps. אבא שאול (אביי's list) says all the lamps come before the קטורת. The five lamps always come before the קטורת.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One should not prepare the lamps
and afterward burn the incense,
rather, he should burn the incense and afterward prepare the lamps.
phrases.notes: The opinion of the רבנן, matching our משנה.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
He prepares the lamps, and afterward burns the incense.
phrases.notes: Matches אביי's list.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא לֹא יֵיטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת וְאַחַר כָּךְ יַקְטִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the dispute claimed in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that אביי's list follows אבא שאול and our משנה follows the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between the רבנן and אבא שאול about the order of the קטורת and the נרות

steps.title: What is the source for אבא שאול's order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason or פסוק supports אבא שאול's view that the lamps are cleaned before the קטורת is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of אבא שאול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אבא שאול holds that cleaning the lamps comes before the קטורת. This sets up the next step, where the answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 13 only told us what each side holds. It did not tell us why. Now the גמרא looks for the source behind אבא שאול's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The תנא who holds that the lamps are cleaned before the קטורת

phrases.english: What is the reason of Abba Shaul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind one side of the disagreement proven in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for אבא שאול's order: lamps first, then קטורת.

steps.title: The verse mentions the lamps first, then the burning
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול learns the order from the פסוק itself: it first says 'when he cleans the lamps' and only afterward says 'he shall burn it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Every morning, when he cleans the lamps,' and afterward 'he shall burn it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אבא שאול follows the order of the words in the פסוק. The פסוק first speaks about cleaning the lamps, and then it speaks about burning the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול reads 'בהיטיבו את הנרות' as the first action. He reads 'יקטירנה' as the next action. So the order of the words in the פסוק tells us the order of the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: When he cleans (prepares) the lamps
He shall burn it (the קטורת)
And afterward / and then

steps.confusionAlert: Both phrases come from the same פסוק about the קטורת. The question is only whether the word 'when' (בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ) means 'after he cleans' (אבא שאול) or something else. The next step begins the רבנן's reading, which continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Every morning
when he cleans the lamps,"
and afterward "he shall burn it."
phrases.notes: The order of the words in the פסוק shows the order of the actions: first the lamps, then the קטורת.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת״, וַהֲדַר ״יַקְטִירֶנָּה״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק puts cleaning the lamps before 'he shall burn it,' so the lamps come first.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the same verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן explain the פסוק, and it begins their answer with 'What is the Torah saying?'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, how do they deal with this פסוק? They say: what is the Torah telling us here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן explain this פסוק, since it seems to support אבא שאול. It then opens their answer with 'מאי קאמר רחמנא', and the explanation itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that the קטורת comes first, so they must read the פסוק differently. The words 'מאי קאמר רחמנא' tell us that the רבנן will explain what the Torah really means here. They will not simply follow the order of the words.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis, how do they answer this?
What is the Merciful One (the Torah) saying?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: A short way of asking: how do the רבנן explain this פסוק?

phrases.english: What is the Merciful One saying:
phrases.notes: This opens the רבנן's reading. The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from אבא שאול's source to the other side, asking how the רבנן handle the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן explain the פסוק that seems to put the lamps before the קטורת.
